{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRCof88AAAABZgsvxA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn7ElzhDHw2M", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn7El", "number": 73, "title": "Implement YM2608 Timer A/B IRQ enables and register-29 reset defaults", "body": "## Problem

The Ap YM2608 model ignores register 29h's individual timer IRQ enables. `Opn::irq()` returns true whenever either timer flag is set, and construction initializes register 29h to zero. Consequently, software cannot suppress timer interrupts through this register.

Evidence: [default state and IRQ calculation](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/9d821b50757801317c6afae5c65d0b08f3c864de/src/sound.rs#L34-L65), [timer flag generation](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/9d821b50757801317c6afae5c65d0b08f3c864de/src/sound.rs#L115-L134), and [sound IRQ routing](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/9d821b50757801317c6afae5c65d0b08f3c864de/src/bus.rs#L310-L315).

This affects DOS sound-driver interrupt control and is a bounded prerequisite for extending OPNA interrupt sources.

## Expected outcome

Implement the following contract for the Ap YM2608:

- Bank-zero register 29h D0/D1 independently enable Timer A/B IRQ output. D7 retains its existing SCH channel-enable role.
- Reset sets D4:D0 to `11111b` and SCH to zero. Reserved bits receive a documented deterministic policy.
- For currently implemented sources, active IRQ is `(timer_flags & register_29 & 03h) != 0`. Recompute after enable changes, including already-pending flags.
- Register 29h changes neither timer progression nor status flags. Register 27h continues to control loading, overflow flag generation and flag clearing. Status reads remain nondestructive.

These semantics follow Yamaha's [YM2608 Application Manual §2-2-1, page 19](https://csclub.uwaterloo.ca/~pbarfuss/YM2608J_Translated.PDF#page=19) and [§2-8-3, page 36](https://csclub.uwaterloo.ca/~pbarfuss/YM2608J_Translated.PDF#page=36), available here as an English transcription/translation.

Keep device output separate from PIC state: disabling a source must not erase an already-latched PIC request or in-service bit. Normal acknowledgement and EOI remain necessary. See Intel's [8259A interrupt sequence and EOI descriptions](https://courses.cs.washington.edu/courses/cse451/25wi/documentation/8259A.pdf#page=7).

## Context and reproduction

Baseline: `9d821b50757801317c6afae5c65d0b08f3c864de`. The supplied context lists no open Issues. Neither the channel-3 improvement nor IDE PR #72 implements this behavior.

A minimal original regression can construct `Opn`, write register 29h=`80h`, program Timer A with 24h=`FFh`, 25h=`03h`, 27h=`05h`, then advance 145 existing guest CPU clocks. Source inspection predicts a set Timer A flag and an incorrectly asserted IRQ. Expected: the flag remains observable while IRQ is inactive. This reproduction was inspected, not executed by the evaluator.

The existing [sound86 test](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/9d821b50757801317c6afae5c65d0b08f3c864de/tests/sound86.rs#L9-L39) writes `83h`, enabling both timer IRQs; it does not cover suppression. Preserve its FM6, board-mask and IRQ assertions, together with the timer/channel-3 tests in `tests/ap.rs`.

Scope is register-29 reset and Timer A/B IRQ gating in the existing core, plus necessary acceptance coverage. Do not add an interrupt framework, change timer frequencies, expose sound on VM, or treat the shared Rust type name `Opn` as evidence that YM2203 implements register 29h.

Remaining OPNA work includes LFO, pan/stereo, rhythm, ADPCM playback/register/IRQ behavior, proprietary rhythm-sample absence, and broader synthesis validation. Unimplemented ADPCM-related flags must not be fabricated to exercise their enable bits. Shared OPN gaps—including CSM keying, combined channel-3 mode, frequency-write latching, prescalers and fuller envelopes—remain separate.

Progress retained: [PR #72](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/pull/72) implements the selected IDE VERIFY completion/residual contract. The Coordinator's [validation record](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/9d821b50757801317c6afae5c65d0b08f3c864de/docs/validation.md#issue-71-ide-read-verify-2026-10-24) reports 294 native integration and 104 production-Wasm browser passes, including disclosed earlier failures and a final alternate-port run. Independent review and remote CI results were not supplied. IDE still needs completed 256-sector PIO acceptance, READ/WRITE completion/error residuals and fuller reset/device interactions.

All 26 supplied inventory scopes and statuses remain unchanged: **partial** cpu-v30, cpu386, protected-mode, memory, pic, pit, dma, rtc, keyboard, mouse, fdc, ide, gdc, egc, pegc, text-cg, display-timing, opn, opna, pcm86, bios, lio and integration; **implemented_unverified** grcg; **unimplemented** paging and fpu. Protected execution, paging and basic x87 remain required. This Issue does not establish complete OPNA accuracy or commercial compatibility.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Add an original focused regression demonstrating the disabled-timer failure on the baseline, record the failure, then implement the contract above without weakening its expectations.
- [ ] Add `opna_irq_*` Rust coverage in `tests/sound86.rs`: exhaust the four timer-flag combinations against all four timer-enable combinations; exercise pending-flag enable/disable transitions, independent timer clearing, clock accumulation across mask changes, repeated status reads, SCH independence, instance isolation and Machine reset. Generate flags through register programming and elapsed clocks.
- [ ] Through existing guest-visible ports, verify sound routing to slave IR4/vector 1Ch: suppression from a clean PIC state, enabled delivery, retained PIC requests after device suppression, acknowledgement/EOI and subsequent recovery. Preserve PCM's independent IRQ contribution, existing board I/O gating and upper-bank isolation. Observe delivery by the next normal scheduler tick; no new timing architecture is required.
- [ ] Add an original MIT bare-metal `guest/opna_irq.asm` probe, offline preparation and checked provenance manifest, following existing probe conventions. Record source/image hashes, assembly command, expected status/IRQ records, guard bytes and a fixed budget of at most 500,000 scheduler slots per boot. Exercise both timers, suppressed and enabled paths, and actual guest-handler execution. No proprietary ROMs, samples or acquired guest binaries are required.
- [ ] Execute that identical source-built image natively and through production release-Wasm at both `/` and `/pc98-rust/`, before and after Machine reset. Require exact result/guard bytes and interrupt counts, PASS without FAIL or emulator/browser errors, unchanged media and compliance with the fixed budget. Hosts may mount, step, reset and inspect outputs; they must not inject flags, interrupts or result bytes.
- [ ] The Coordinator runs `cargo test --locked --test sound86 opna_irq_`, the complete `sound86`, `ap`, `music` and `pic` targets, then the repository-required `cargo test --locked`, Clippy with warnings denied, formatting, media/font reproducibility, whitespace checks and `npm test`, using the README's licensed fixture prerequisites. Preserve existing DOS/application, VM, audio, hardware and six-game assertions and execution budgets.
- [ ] Wire the new offline probe into existing acceptance CI and document reproduction, the bounded contract and remaining gaps. The PR reports exact commands, outcomes, failures and omissions, attributing Coordinator and CI evidence separately. Complete review and all mandatory checks before merge; this evaluator performs no builds, tests, fixture preparation or repository changes.

## Optional validation

None.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
